mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,300K units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1300 for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes at 5% significance, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98 for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede a recession in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the effective federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary regime, which historically coincides with equity market stress and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 7% YoY for four consecutive months, alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) growth below zero for two consecutive quarters, signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 7% YoY for four months AND GDPC1 < 0% QoQ for two quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 250K for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the trigger does not precede a positive earnings revision cycle in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102 for three consecutive months and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,400K for two consecutive months signals a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and construction, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 102 for three months AND HOUST > 1400 for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede an official NBER expansion.
